comment: [SOURCE-DEVIATION 2026-08-10 — week grid becomes a per-day submission] The source PDF is a WEEKLY
paper sheet: 16 check rows x 7 day columns (Monday..Sunday), each column a Defective/Okay pair,
with a single 'Week Commencing' date in the header block. That 2-D matrix has NO representation in
this system and cannot be added: a checklist group (forms/meta-schema.json) is
additionalProperties:false over {key,label,scale,comment_per_item,items}, and a checklist item
files exactly ONE {response, comment} pair in BOTH renderers (safety_reports/form_pdf.py and
safety_portal/src/forms/FormRenderer.tsx). The faithful digital equivalent is ONE submission per
operating day keyed to the work_date envelope field; the WEEK is reconstituted downstream by
weekly_generate -> form_pdf.merge_pdfs (Sat->Fri ascending), which is exactly what the paper grid's
seven columns were. The rejected alternatives, for the record: 7 items per check (bucket_mon,
bucket_tue, ...) would 7x the item count and destroy the source's semantics; an 8-column
repeating_table would make every check-item LABEL an operator-editable text box, so nothing pins
'Engine Oil Level/Leaks' to row 1 and the sheet stops being a fixed inspection artifact.
The source's 'Week Commencing' header field is deliberately NOT carried over. It exists on paper
only to say which Monday-to-Sunday sheet you are holding, and it actively CONFLICTS here: ITS
buckets and compiles on a SATURDAY-to-Friday week (safety_week / weekly_generate), so an
operator-typed Monday date would sit on a signed page beside a packet whose week starts two days
earlier, and the two can never agree. work_date already determines the week unambiguously. No
check item was added, dropped, reordered or reworded.
[SCALE] 'Okay'/'Defective' is the source's own two-state vocabulary (the paper form's tick and
cross columns), not the ['OK','NO','N/A'] used by the telehandler variant or the
['OK','NOT OK','N/A'] used by the skid-steer variant — those two already disagree with each other,
and each was transcribed from its own source. The source offers no N/A box, so none is invented;
items are optional, and an inapplicable check is left unanswered exactly as it is left blank on
paper.
[LEGAL FLOOR] The closing lock/tag-out static_text is NOT on the source PDF. It is the
equipment-preinspection PARENT requirement (safety_portal/required-content.json:
'ALWAYS lock/tag-out unsafe equipment' plus required_signature_inputs_min 1), carried
byte-identically from equipment-skid-steer-v1 and equipment-telehandler-v1.

sections.text: All checks must be carried out in line with Manufacturer's Operators Manual.
Report any problems found to your supervisor/employer. ALWAYS lock/tag-out unsafe equipment.
